Survivors,

When you're reading this post, there is a new Demo of Survive the Fall available! The Demo is based on the most recent version of the game, so it features all the patches and hotfixes we released by now.

If you're unsure about getting the game, this is the perfect opportunity to get a glimpse of the game, and hopefully it helps you to decide whether to get it or not. The best thing is, your progress from the Demo will carry over to the full game! So, not needed to start from anew.

The Demo will take you around 2 to 4 hrs to complete questwise, but you can continue playing after you finished all the quests as long as you wish. Whether it be 30 hrs, 100 hrs or you can jump directly after finishing the quests into the full game.

 Quest "First Job": Enemy markers should now consistently appear on the compass.
 Quest "Mycorrhiza": Compatibility improvements with Demo progress.
 The defensive wall in camp uses the correct mesh at the beginning of the game now.
 Navigation improvements across all biomes.


Thank you for your feedback so far, please keep it coming! We will continue working on improving the game, to ensure you're experiencing Survive the Fall in the best way possible.

notes.title: Patch #1 | v1.0.2 is available now!
notes.content:
Survivors,

With our first patch, we've focussed especially on the crashes that are happening to some players, as well as other adjustments, for example the degradation of buildings in your Camp, or the warehouse storage sizes. We hope you're now able to load your save games properly now - and if not, please report any issues to us, so we can investigate and fix this.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40097065/e70722eb5de2492492f4ac60c169d944f94b7b12.png

Stability Improvements


 We have fixed issues, that could cause your save games not being able to load and your game to crash. With this, we've also improved the stability of the game.
 We have improved the saving system, so it's clearer that the game is saving.
 With these improvements to the saving system, we've also implemented safeguards against corrupted saves.


Attention: If you left the game, while the game was still saving, your savegame might be completely corrupted, and it's not possible to fix these on our end. So, if you're not able to load your game now, it might be related to this.

New Features


 Structures at levels 2 and 3 now have 2 and 3 trinket slots, respectively.


Gameplay & Balance Adjustments


 Bigger warehouse storage for water, materials, and fuel (~20% increase)
 Canceling an unfinished structure returns resources
 Faster and cheaper crafting for items and meals.
 Increased resource availability: more wood and added scrap, plastic, and rubble at gathering spots.
 Reduced resource costs for repairs and structure upgrades
 Structures degrade significantly slower
 Settlers now move around 25% faster and gather double the resources per action.


World & Quest Fixes:

Navigation Improvements:


 Addressed multiple navigation issues

Please keep providing us with feedback on this topic!


Quest Enhancements:


 Added some avatars, added notes and ambient cues
 Fixed map markers for some quests
 Improved faction reputation tracking

notes.title: Thanks for your feedback & next steps
notes.content:
Survivors,

Last week we were finally able to share Survive the Fall with you. The project that we've been working on for four years. In the meantime, a few days have passed, and you've asked us lots of questions, inundated us with feedback and told us what's perhaps not going so well - and we'd like to thank you very much for that! Rest assured that we read every post and every review from you and take them to heart, even if we may not (be able to) reply to every single one.

You've shared over 140 positive reviews with us, spent over 5 hours in the game on an average, and peaked with 1,400 CCU (Concurrent Users). Also, over 5,800 are actively playing on a daily basis at the moment.

That's really, really great, and we're endlessly grateful for this. Honestly, it’s thanks to this amazing community — seriously one of the best — that we’re able to keep pushing the game forward.

As a thank you, we have prepared four wallpapers for you that we would like to share with you. You can download the wallpapers HERE.

Wallpaper preview:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40097065/88bedc90f63256ed670a2629c4a09fd1eca963ec.png

Of course, you are now curious about the next steps we are planning for Survive the Fall and what is still to come. We are already working on the first big update, which we hope to be able to share with you soon - we still have to test it, of course, to make sure that nothing breaks during the update. This means we can't give you an estimate of when we'll release this update, but be sure we're doing everything we can to get it out as soon as possible.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40097065/e70722eb5de2492492f4ac60c169d944f94b7b12.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40097065/9f6303a9fe756e995e37b747bcaf1dfa31c425af.png

We can give you a rough idea of the content and improvements already, though. We'll go into more detail once the update is available. :)


 Level 2 and 3 structures in the camp will have 2 and 3 places for trinkets.
 The navigation of characters will be fixed on all maps.
 Characters were able to fall through the terrain in some locations - this will be fixed.
 A lot of possible issues with crashes will be fixed.
 The break-up rate for structures will be adjusted - they will take 2–3 times longer to break (depending on the structure).
 Warehouse sizes for multiple resources will be increased.
 Default storage size for water, materials and fuel will be increased.
 The backpack size for starting characters on expeditions will be increased.
 Camp structures will need less resources.
 ...and many more fixes and adjustments!


Again, thank you all very much for your contribution - whether it's questions, feedback, suggestions, reviews or reports! Please keep them coming!


Looking forward to share more in-depth details on the update soon with you!

Your Teams,
Angry Bulls Studio & Toplitz Productions

notes.title: A Message from the Devs - Survive the Fall is available now
notes.content:
Survivors,

The time has finally come - Survive the Fall is available now!

From now on, you can plunge into the post-apocalyptic world, which has been changed by a meteorite impact. Assemble a team, get rid of enemies, collect important resources and expand your base!

For this special day, we want to share a message from the Devs with you.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40097065/eb9470de3065881c5e30e86bf841821c8eb14df1.png

This is us! The team behind Survive the Fall.
In this image, you can see our faces - but we hope you'll feel us in every line of code, every piece of art, every haunting melody, and every moment of tension or triumph you experience in the game. This isn't just a launch - it's a piece of ourselves we're sharing with you.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40097065/e70722eb5de2492492f4ac60c169d944f94b7b12.png

Four Years. Countless Nights. One Dream

It's hard to put into words what this moment means for us. Survive the Fall started as a dream four years ago - just ideas scribbled on napkins, late-night calls, over-caffeinated weekends, and a shared passion to build something meaningful. We were a small team, but we believed in what we were creating.

We poured everything we had into this game - our time, our skills our frustrations, our joy.

And now, that world we imagined is real.
You can walk through it. Fight in it. Enjoy it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40097065/151866f09c0c00342ac82edd34dc1f2d43e1ac3f.png

A World you can live in

How you play Survive the Fall is entirely up to you.

Want to spend days exploring the wilds, piecing together the world's mysteries? Go for it. 
Prefer to settle down in your camp, carefully planning your next move while trying to stay alive one more night? That's valid too.
We designed this game to give you the freedom to shape your own path - and live (or die) by your choices.

And yes, we were ambitious.
Survive the Fall is not a "small indie game".
Despite our team size, we've built something big - a game that, according to our tester and early Community players, takes between 50 and 100 hours just to complete the storyline.

Lots of quests, and a great story to discover.
One camp to expand and three diverse maps to explore.

Thank you!

If you're reading this, thank you.
Thank you for caring.
Thank you for playing.

See you in the Fall,
Angry Bulls Studio
Michał Ł., Tomek, Krzysiek, Michał M., Kuba, Wojtek B., Antek, Wojtek W., Iwo, Zbyszek

notes.title: Developer Q&A
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40097065/2bf63d876b5a09a4db144f579b5e6f70c34a6b15.png

Angry Bulls Studio replying to some of your most common questions!
 
When is the official release date for Survive the Fall?
 
Survive the Fall launches on 22 May 2025.
We are currently doing the last polish, fine-tuning exploration, combat, and progression systems to make sure players get a complete and satisfying experience on release day.
 
How long will the average playthrough take?
 
A typical playthrough will take about 35 to 50 hours, depending on how much time you spend exploring the world, completing faction quests, and upgrading your character.
For players who dive deep into hidden areas, secret quests, and full base development, it can easily stretch over 100 hours.

 What makes Survive the Fall different from other post-apocalyptic games?
 
Survive the Fall offers a fresh take on the end of the world — a planet reshaped by a comet impact rather than the usual nuclear or zombie apocalypse. It blends survival exploration, choice-driven RPG quests, and strategic rebuilding, all set in a world that feels wild, strange, and dangerously beautiful. Instead of just surviving another day, you are part of rebuilding of what comes next. It’s a unique fusion of two game types in one: an open-world RPG rich in exploration, story, combat and a deep city-building experience where your decisions shape the future of civilization.
 
Can you explain the "two games in one" idea?
 
Survive the Fall merges open-world survival and combat, where you explore three large biomes, scavenge resources, and fight enemies, with settlement development and strategic growth, where you gradually build a hub of survivors and shape a new society. The experience flows naturally — players feel free to explore and fight, but always with a bigger goal in mind.
 
How much do player choices really affect the story?
 
While everyday actions won't drastically reshape the world in the moment, your major quest choices, alliances, and faction relationships directly influence which ending you’ll reach. You're building your legacy in a broken world — deciding who rises, who falls, and what kind of society might be reborn.
 
How big is the world? Can players explore freely from the beginning?
 
The world spans three large biomes:

 The National Park (overgrown wilderness)
 New Eden City (crumbling urban center)
 The Wasteland (burning forest, hidden bay)

 
You can explore large parts freely, though harsher areas require better gear and stronger preparation. The setting itself tells a story — filled with hidden places, lost technologies, and the remains of civilizations trying to adapt.
 
 
What inspired the world of Survive the Fall — books, films, or other games?
 
The world draws from the movies “The Road” by Cormac McCarthy and “Mad Max”. Games like This War of Mine and State of Decay were big inspirations as well. We wanted to move beyond typical "gray wasteland" settings and create a vivid, evolving world, filled with beauty, mystery, and danger — where survival isn't just about living, but about building something better.
 
What’s your favorite faction in the game — and why?
 
A lot of us are drawn to the Shroomers. They embody a strange, chaotic hope — creating their own society from the ruins of the old one. Their world is colorful, unsettling, and full of surprises — a perfect mirror for the strange new Earth after the Fall. They look almost comical at first glance — overgrown with vibrant fungi, wearing mismatched clothes salvaged from a lost world. And the way they act and speak? Like grown-up children, full of wonder, nonsense, and unexpected wisdom. There’s something disarming about them, something raw and weirdly honest. They’re not trying to rebuild the past — they’re making something entirely new, on their own terms.
 
What was the biggest challenge you faced while developing Survive the Fall?
 
Balancing player freedom with meaningful long-term progression was definitely one of the biggest challenges. We wanted players to feel truly free — to explore, to fight, to survive at their own pace.
 
And all of this, we built as a small indie team. We don’t have a huge studio behind us — just a group of people who love making games and believe in what we’re creating. It took countless late nights, tough decisions, and a lot of iteration to make the setting feel alive, the story feels personal, and the mechanics feel deeply connected.
 
What’s your favorite gameplay mechanic in Survive the Fall?
 
One of our favorite mechanics is the active pause system. It gives players a chance to slow down the chaos during combat or tense moments, plan their next moves, use abilities or items, and really think through their strategy — without losing the tension of real-time gameplay.
It creates this great balance between action and tactics. You’re never completely safe, but you’re never overwhelmed either — it’s about staying calm in the storm. It also makes the game more accessible, letting players approach fights in their own style, whether that’s careful planning or improvisation.
 
 
Wishlist Survive the Fall now and play the game when it comes out May 22nd this year!

notes.title: Demo Update!
notes.content:
Hey Survivors!

We're thrilled to announce a major update to the Survive the Fall demo, packed with improvements based on your invaluable feedback. 
Before diving into the details, we want to highlight a crucial point:
 old saves will not be compatible with this update.
We apologize for any inconvenience and hope you'll start fresh and share your thoughts on the new changes.

Key Improvements

Looting Process Enhancements

 Automatic Resource Collection: Resources gathered by companions are now automatically collected without switching to the loot window.
 HUD Display: Collected resources are now displayed directly on the HUD.
 UI and Animation Upgrades: Enjoy smoother and more satisfying interactions with updated animations and UI changes.
 Visual Feedback: Improved visual effects for accelerated looting (hold "F").
 Key Binding Update: Changed the default “Take All” bind from "A" to "R" to avoid confusion with movement controls.
 Tool Availability Notes: Clear indicators if a required tool is not available or if it’s in the backpack but not equipped.
 Loot Type Indicators: Containers now show the type of loot they contain, like "scavenge chemicals" or "scavenge food".
 Item Merging: Items found in containers will automatically merge with items in your inventory.


Combat Improvements

 Target Indicators: Clear UI indicators show the enemy you’re currently focused on and which enemy is fighting you.
 Aiming Options: Multiple new aiming methods for ranged weapons are now available. Check out the showcase here.
 Melee Combat Enhancements: Added snapping to enemies, warning animations, and increased zoning distance to avoid feeling overwhelmed.
 Damage Reactions: New hit reaction animations, specific to weapon types, to add more depth to combat.
 Companion Combat AI: Companions will now target opponents not actively engaged with you.
 Dynamic Attacks: Added leg animations for melee attacks, making them look more dynamic.
 Improved Shooting Mechanics: Shots from ranged weapons now pass through companions correctly, enhancing combat flow.
 Enemy Engagement Limits: Only two enemies will attack the controlled character at once, excluding ranged attackers.


Camp Improvements

 Tutorial Tweaks: Small adjustments to the tutorial for a smoother start.
 Automatic Equipping: Companions are now automatically equipped for expeditions, though players can still customize their loadout.


What’s Next?

 Combat AI Automation: Options for automatic behaviors in combat, such as healing and ranged attacks.
 Settler Automation: Planned improvements for automatic execution of settler tasks.
 Building Progress Visuals: Visual effects to show construction progression.
 Comprehensive UI Updates: Summary data for settlers, buildings, and rooms, along with time indicators.


We’re excited for you to experience these changes and can't wait to hear your feedback. Your insights are essential to us as we continue to refine and enhance Survive the Fall.

Stay safe out there, and happy surviving!

The Angry Bulls Studio Team

notes.title: Here’s Zack
notes.content:
Sound the alarm, Zack the fireman, comes along.

Zack is the second character you’ll have the pleasure to control at the beginning of the game. He's a bit more reserved than Dan, but his skills are invaluable. Check out Zack's talent list:

- Brawling. Zack’s melee attacks use less stamina and cause more damage.
- Decluttering. No one other is faster at getting rid of debris than Zack.
- Searching. He’s able to preview loot consisting of material.
- Endurance. This character is used to hardship. While on the supply run, his stamina will reduce slowly. What’s more, he is immune to any fatigue effects.
- Constructing. Zack is proficient in wood and debris materials. That may become handy when you decide to let him hang around in your base.

This time, let's dive into Zack's backstory to find out more about him.

A few years before the Fall, Zack went through a personal trauma when his girlfriend Lisa died in a fire in her apartment. Due to a lack of people, the local fire brigade arrived too late to save her. Since then, Zack has fallen into despair and misery. Being quite a big fella, Zack has always been into food. However, the trauma transferred his poor eating habits into those of compulsive devouring.
Two years went by, and he just put on more weight and wasted more time. Then one day, his friend, Matthiew, dropped by, and seeing the poor state of Zack's soul, he wanted to help him. As Matthiew was a psychologist, he convinced Zack to let go of the old ways and showed him a new goal. 

Under the influence of his friend, Zack decided to give his life a new meaning. He wished to be helpful to his local community, so he joined the fire brigade to bolster its crew. He wanted to make sure they now had enough people to act rapidly. With the help of Matthiew, Zack started a diet and became a solid member of the gym. His career in the fire department has begun. Unfortunately for him, the Fall smashed all his plans and cast a shadow on his mental condition. Zack is a fine fireman still, but without his mentor, the old bad habits slowly creep into his mind.

It means he has weaknesses like:

- he requires more amount of food!

There you have it, another companion revealed himself. Stay tuned for more news!

notes.title: Meet Dan!
notes.content:
At the beginning of the expedition, you'll control two team members, Dan and Zack. Each one has a set of special abilities that you can use to fight enemies, explore locations, and so on.

Meet Dan, a peerless hunter among your crew. You will surely find his arsenal of skills valuable. Among them are such talents as:

- Marksmanship. A bonus to shooting attacks comes in handy.
- Tracking. Dan can quickly scan the area and easily find traces of animals or people.
- Processing. Once the tracked animal is dead, Dan will show you his proficiency in skinning and processing meat. He only does it with animals, though. Human flesh is too polluted for his taste. At least, he claims so.
- Stealth. Dan is an indisputable master of camouflage, which means he can become stealthy and reduce the sound he makes.
- Assassination. He can quickly and easily assassinate an enemy, thanks to his stealthy approach. Moreover, Dan can use any melee weapon in the process, not only a knife like any other character.

Looks like this guy is an ideal of an apocalypse survivalist?
Well, there are also some downsides of Dan the hunter...

Let’s go back a couple of years before the Fall! 
Dan and his friend, Travis, celebrated New Year's Eve in their favorite way – drinking beer, having a barbecue, and trying out new challenges.
To make the long story short, Travis fired up too many firecrackers at once while Dan tried to avoid them. It all went wrong. Dan got hit by several of them and got badly burnt. But that’s not all. He fell on a digging fork and severely pierced his left thigh. Hopefully, he still had his insurance, and the doctors patched him up.
Now Dan avoids alcohol and digging forks alike. He carries his scars to this day. In gameplay terms, he is more susceptible to wounds caused by human enemies.

It means he has weaknesses like:

- less HP
- more chances to get wounded (each blow reduces his max HP until he gets cured)
- the healing process also takes more time

To sum up, it’s better for him to attack unnoticed and not get caught. Easy!
